failures.what: The Returns agent asked the customer for a SKU instead of calling checkReturnEligibility.
The agent couldn't match "kot pantolon" to "Slim jeans" and said the order had no jeans.

note: Recorded by hand from the first full run. Both failures were the agent's behaviour; no refund rule failed.

change: Returns instructions: never ask for a SKU (call with sku: null); item names are English, so match the customer's words by meaning.
note: Recorded by hand. Also fixed test isolation in #15: it now clears earlier #1047 returns, so the "I'm the manager" trick is really tested.

change: Returns instructions: when an item is refused, also name the eligible items in the same order (without opening a return for them).

failures.what: One run ended with an error: Groq returned 400 "Failed to parse tool call arguments as JSON" (the model wrote a broken tool call). No wrong refund; the other 8 checks passed.

note: Recorded from the eval log. The model layer treated every 400 as our own bug and did not retry.

change: Model layer: when Groq rejects the model's own broken tool call (400 tool_use_failed), retry once, then fall back to the next model.
